name: Oxalidaceae

lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach project Oxalis through trifoliolate leaves, 5-merous flowers, 10 stamens in two lengths and a 5-locular capsule that ejects seeds, then leave fine species separation to a five-taxon comparison.

project_scope.note: Project taxa: O. drummondii, O. dillenii, O. albicans, O. stricta and O. violacea. All five names are accepted current concepts; exact local-native status is species-lane work, especially O. stricta.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Start with the leaf and flower together: project Oxalis has three leaflets, usually with a notched or heartlike leaflet outline, and a radial 5-petaled flower.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Herbs, often with bulbs, tubers, rhizomes or fleshy roots. Project leaves are palmately trifoliolate and may fold at night or under stress.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Five sepals and five petals; 10 stamens in two whorls/length classes, commonly 5 long and 5 short; superior 5-locular ovary with 5 styles.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Loculicidal capsule; mature seeds may be forcibly ejected by a fleshy elastic outer seed coat.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Trifoliolate woodsorrel leaf + 5 petals + 10 unequal stamens + 5-part capsule is the family/genus package.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: trifoliolate leaf → 5-part flower → long/short stamen pair → 5 styles/ovary → capsule/ejection → five-species color/habit card → Geraniaceae contrast
visual_lesson.intro: Woodsorrels become much easier once the flower center is learned: ten stamens alternate long-short around five styles.

steps.title: 1 · Read the three leaflets
steps.look_for: Three palmately arranged leaflets, often obcordate/notched at the tip.

steps.title: 2 · Count five petals and ten stamens
steps.look_for: Five petals around ten stamens arranged in two length classes.

steps.title: 3 · Find the five styles
steps.look_for: Five styles/stigmas arising from a superior 5-locular ovary.

steps.title: 4 · Follow the flower to an explosive capsule
steps.look_for: Five-valved capsule releasing seeds abruptly when mature.

steps.title: 5 · Build the five-species comparison
steps.look_for: Purple/pink geophytic O. drummondii and O. violacea versus yellow-flowered O. dillenii/O. stricta and pale O. albicans, with habit/hair/underground-organ characters added.
steps.why_it_matters: Prevents color-only species IDs while organizing the pool.

comparisons.title: Oxalidaceae vs Geraniaceae
comparisons.rule: Both can have 5-petaled flowers, but project Oxalis has trifoliolate leaves, 10 stamens in two lengths and a 5-locular capsule; familiar Geraniaceae has a long-beaked schizocarp splitting into five awned mericarps.

visual_lesson.caveat: Do not separate the yellow woodsorrels by flower color alone. O. dillenii and O. stricta especially need stem/hair/rhizome characters in the species lane.

genera.fast_cue: trifoliolate woodsorrel + 5 petals + 10 unequal stamens + 5-part capsule

taxonomy_reconciliation.note: Accepted; native range includes central/southern Texas.
Accepted; current Kew range treatment requires species-level local-status care rather than assuming Texas nativity.

visual_targets.annotation_goal: habit, flower color, hair and underground-organ differences
